record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports outcomes from orthogonalizing model weights with a difference-in-means refusal direction. This tests practical removal using a weight edit, rather than the original activation-level intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports successful results for six models and says DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B did not refuse even at baseline. Direction-layer and depth values are reported, but are selection/location information rather than separate behavioural outcomes. No addition or general-capability results are reported.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal-removal outcomes from orthogonalizing weights with a difference-in-means direction on six released instruct/chat models. This bears on V2 and on the ablation part of V1. The evidence is checkmarks only, with no rates, baselines or capability measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The README claims abliteration works on all standard-transformer instruct models. It says the refusal direction sits at 41%-67% of depth, consistently across vendors, countries and training pipelines. It also says the direction's position matters more than its strength: the layer with the largest statistic is often not the one that controls refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction, but applies it through weight orthogonalization rather than reporting the original activation-level ablation and addition tests. This is a tool repository, not a reported reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different direction layers and depths across models.
record.problems: The README provides checkmarks rather than quantitative refusal outcomes, gives no baseline refusal rates for the successful cases, and reports no uncertainty, controls, or general-capability evaluation. The code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for direction-layer/depth values: the README presents these as direction locations, not distinct behavioural results. The file list contains no stated result files.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; activation-level ablation at every layer and position, reported separately; retention of general abilities. Only the outcome of the weight-edit removal is reported.
Quantitative refusal rates before and after the edit; capability or coherence cost of the edited models.
All. The 'consistent across vendors and workflows' remark concerns direction depth, not transfer of one direction.
All. The consistency claim across training pipelines is asserted without a controlled comparison.
All. The one reasoning-distilled model did not refuse at baseline, so it was not tested.

missing.what: article.md may contain refusal rates, examples or capability observations behind the checkmarks; it is not in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Hobbyist tool repo, not peer-reviewed. The 'fast' script orthogonalizes top-N candidate directions and keeps the one that validates. Success is therefore partly a selection outcome, and evaluation uses few prompts (try-n 8, eval-n 20). The README notes that the largest difference-in-means statistic often fails to mark the effective layer. This is a method-sensitivity caveat on direction selection, not a measured result. No Llama result is reported, despite the classic script targeting Llama-3-8B.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports weight-edit removal only. It does not report projecting the direction out of every layer and position, adding the direction, or measuring retained general abilities.
No quantitative refusal rates or general-capability measurements are reported.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No measurement separating harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No test of transfer across languages, base/instruct stages, or model variants.
The README asserts consistency across training workflows but reports no controlled comparison of refusal training methods or stages.
No test of the direction in reasoning models.
